conventions.entity: The subject the disputed fact is about (product/system/service/feature).
conventions.attribute: The specific property, policy, or quantity in dispute.
conventions.old_value: The value superseded by the newer source (the 'earlier' figure in the gold answer).
conventions.new_value: The current/applied value (the one the gold answer says to use).
conventions.old_span: Verbatim substring of the older source document that states old_value.
conventions.new_span: Verbatim substring of the newer source document that states new_value.
conventions.supersession_sentence: Verbatim sentence in the newer document that explicitly marks the change; UNSURE if no explicit marker exists.
conventions.temporal_quality: T1 = BOTH documents of the pair carry structured date metadata AND the newer document's date is day-precision (a full date in the filename or a dated header field) so it can order the pair on its own; T2 = anything less (structured metadata absent from either document, or present but year-only in the newer document), with in-text dates treated as corroboration only; T3 = no ordering signal.
conventions.expected_state: CANON if a clear supersession makes new_value canon; CONTESTED if the conflict is unresolved; UNSURE if not determinable from the text.
conventions.old_value_literal: The single number/name/phrase from old_value that distinguishes it; must appear verbatim inside old_span.
conventions.new_value_literal: The single number/name/phrase from new_value that distinguishes it; must appear verbatim inside new_span.
conventions.new_doc_mentions_old_value: true if old_value_literal also occurs in the newer document's text (the superseded value is re-stated there); false otherwise.
conventions.composite: true if the newer document extends the older value (adds/refines it, or keeps the older value valid/supported) rather than contradicting it; false for a straight replacement.
conventions.seeding: Seeding writes one assertion per document: the newer document asserts the new value only. The old value is never seeded as a claim from the newer document; new_doc_mentions_old_value only flags that the newer document also references it.
